title: Writing learning objectives with Bloom's taxonomy

params.text:
What is a learning objective?

A learning objective says what the learner will be able to do after the lesson, in words you can observe.

Bloom's revised taxonomy (2001) sorts thinking into six levels, from simplest to most complex: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create.

params.question: Which statement is a learning objective?

answers.text: Learners will be able to list the six levels of Bloom's taxonomy.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Right: it names what the learner will do, and the result can be observed.

answers.text: The lesson is about Bloom's taxonomy.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes the topic, not what the learner will be able to do.
Enjoyment cannot be observed or tested, so it is not an objective.

params.text:
Remember and Understand

Remember means recalling facts. Verbs: define, list, name, identify.

Understand means explaining ideas in your own words. Verbs: summarise, classify, explain, describe.

params.question: Which verb belongs to the Understand level?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: List is a Remember verb: it asks for recall, not explanation.
Right: a summary shows the learner has grasped the idea in their own words.
Name is a Remember verb: it asks for recall of a fact.

params.text:
Apply and Analyze

Apply means using knowledge in a new situation. Verbs: use, solve, calculate, demonstrate.

Analyze means breaking something into parts and seeing how they relate. Verbs: compare, differentiate, organise, examine.

params.question: A learner must calculate the total cost of an order using a price list. Which level is this?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Remember would be recalling the price list, not using it to work something out.
Right: the learner uses known information to solve a new problem.
Create would mean building something new, such as a price list of their own.

params.text:
Evaluate and Create

Evaluate means judging something against criteria. Verbs: justify, assess, critique, recommend.

Create means putting parts together into a new whole. Verbs: design, plan, compose, produce.

params.question: Which verb belongs to the Evaluate level?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Right: to justify, the learner judges a choice against stated criteria.
Design is a Create verb: it makes something new rather than judging it.

params.text:
Writing a good objective

A good objective names the learner, one observable verb, the content, and the standard expected.

Example: Learners will be able to classify five sample questions by Bloom level, with at least four correct.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Understand cannot be seen directly, so there is no way to check it. Pick an observable verb.

answers.text: Students will be able to classify five sample questions by Bloom level, with at least four correct.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Right: an observable verb, a clear task and a standard to meet.
Learn names no task and no standard, so it cannot be checked.

params.text:
Common mistakes

Avoid vague verbs such as know, understand and learn. Keep one main verb per objective, and match the level to the assessment you plan.

params.question: The objective says: Learners will know the six levels. What is the main problem?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Length is not the problem here; the verb is.

answers.text: Know cannot be observed directly, so it is hard to assess.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Right: change it to an observable verb such as list or classify.
It does name a topic, the six levels; the verb is what needs changing.
